newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy Ross meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's special envoy arrived on Thursday for talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on a crisis threatening Middle East peace talks, officials said.
The envoy, Dennis Ross, earlier met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Morocco to try to rescue talks foundering over a resurgence of Jewish settlement and Palestinian guerrilla violence.
Israeli-Palestinian relations were plunged into turmoil last week when the Jewish state began building a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinians protesting at the settlement decision have clashed with Israeli soldiers throughout the West Bank, and an Islamic suicide bomber blew himself up in Tel Aviv on Friday, killing three women.

Netanyahu's cabinet secretary Danny Naveh said just before the meeting began "We hope this mission will help us return to the peace process track, the diplomatic process, without violence and terror, without use of violence and terror by (Arafat's) Palestinian Authority."
Israel has charged that Arafat effectively gave a "green light" for violence directed at Israel. Palestinians maintain Israel sparked the bloodshed with its settlement move.
Naveh told reporters that if the parties could revive the battered peace process "this will certainly be something of great importance, and we will hear in a couple of minutes."

Arriving in Jerusalem after what he called "very thorough" talks with Arafat, Ross was taken into Netanyahu's official residence through a side entrance, avoiding a waiting crowd of reporters, photographers and film crews.
